title: MADE x Barbican
address: Barbican, Level G Hub Space,, Silk Street, London, EC2Y 8DS
verdict: Immersive interiors takeover inside the Barbican itself. Long opening hours and a landmark brutalist setting.
description: To celebrate the launch of their interiors collection in collaboration with the Barbican, MADE have created an immersive installation in the iconic institution for LDF26.

title: Sanctum of Renewal
address: Hart Shoreditch, 61-67 Great Eastern Street, London, EC2A 3HU
verdict: Immersive art takeover of a hotel restaurant. Long hours make it easy to fit in, moody and photogenic.
description: Hart Shoreditch is partnering with contemporary urban artist Mali Mowcka to create the exhibition 'Sanctum of Renewal'. This immersive spatial intervention will convert the hotel's restaurant UBA into a contemporary sacred space, a living temple where matter, energy, and perception are in constant movement.

title: slowform presents Rest at Café Vins
address: Café Vins, 1 Marlborough Court, Carnaby, London, W1F 7EE
verdict: A tray and homeware collection shown inside a café. Pleasant if you are stopping for a drink anyway.
description: For London Design Festival 2026, slowform presents Rest, a new tray collection developed with MSSR Works, alongside a selection of slowform garments and objects for daily life at Café Vins in Soho from 17–20 September.

title: The Point of Unity and Soul
address: St Paul's Cathedral, St Paul's Churchyard, London, EC4M 8AD
verdict: Light sculpture and audiovisual piece inside St Paul's Cathedral. Big atmosphere, free, easy win.
description: Presented within the historic setting of St Paul’s, the audiovisual installation, "Soul", and immersive light sculpture, "The Point of Unity", bring contemporary light and media art into dialogue with the Cathedral’s longstanding role as a place of worship, gathering and reflection.

title: The Secret Garden of Silk
venue: Lansei China London Pop-Up — The Secret Garden
address: Lansei China London Pop-Up — The Secret Garden, 2 Blenheim Crescent, Notting Hill, London, W11 2NN
verdict: Live silk embroidery with free hands-on tasters. Tactile and interactive, a real activity not just looking.
description: Step into Lansei China’s Secret Garden of Silk, where Ronghua flowers and Shu silk embroidery unfold through live making, tactile displays and free hands-on tasters. Discover how silk, wire and thread are transformed into flowers, ornaments and miniature gardens.

title: Craft x Tech Tokai Project
address: Victoria & Albert Museum, Medieval & Renaissance, Room 64b, The Simon Sainsbury Gallery, Cromwell Road, London, SW7 2RL
verdict: Japanese craft-meets-technology installation inside the V&A. Strong visuals, teen-friendly venue.
description: Craft x Tech Tokai Project returns to LDF for its second edition. The initiative reinterprets Japan’s Tokai regions' centuries-old traditions, bringing together creatives from six artisan regions, with each artisan collaborating with internationally acclaimed designers.

title: Have You Seen The Light?
address: Tom Dixon Global Flagship Shop, 4-10 Bagley Walk, London, N1C 4DH
verdict: Tom Dixon's full lighting takeover of his Coal Drops Yard flagship. Bold, big-name, and next to plenty of food and shops.
description: Tom Dixon returns to London Design Festival with a complete takeover of the brand’s Coal Drops Yard flagship in King’s Cross. Following debuts in Milan and Copenhagen, the festival marks the first time the complete AW26 collection will be shown together in London, as well as early look at the SS27 collection.

title: WAX 2026
address: The Wax Building, 4 Garden Walk, London, EC2A 3EQ
verdict: Four floors of eclectic design brands in a former Victorian building. Lots to see fast, strong Shoreditch energy.
description: WAX 2026 brings together the resident  brands COZMO, TAMART, MINIMALUX, AND LIGHTMASS^ with a roster of collaborators and friends across the design community. Set over four floors, in a former Victorian factory, 2026 marks its third successful year.

title: your golf course made my GPU by Sam Ghantous
address: V&A, Cromwell Rd, London SW7 2RL, London, SW2 2RL
verdict: Tech-and-nature themed installation on sand, silicon and computing, inside the V&A. Title alone should hook gamer teens.
description: Digital life is mineral. In your golf course made my GPU, Sam Ghantous explores the entanglement between earth and technology through the second most abundant of earthly elements: silica, or sand.

title: Flukette Housewarming
address: 353, 353, Portobello Road, Notting Hill, London, W10 5SA
verdict: Cosy immersive home installation on Portobello Road. Pleasant, photogenic, quick visit.
description: Step inside Flukette Housewarming, an immersive home installation celebrating craftsmanship, curiosity and the little things that make a house feel like home.

title: The World Ends: Bangkok International Design Expo 2026
verdict: Listed on the LDF site but physically in Bangkok. Not reachable today.
description: If the world of design were to end today, what should emerge next? As technology accelerates and environmental, economic and social forces reshape our lives, inherited systems are no longer enough. THE WORLD ENDS: invites us to question what comes next, imagine new possibilities for tomorrows — and CREATE WHAT MATTERS.
excluded_reason: Physically located in Bangkok, not reachable on foot today.

title: Stoneline Gallery Launch 'Alchemy of Perception'
address: Stoneline Experience Centre & Gallery, 132 Wigmore Street, London, W1U 3SD
verdict: Launch event for a stone and surfaces showroom. Trade-oriented, low teen interest.
description: Join Stoneline in a week of activations to celebrate the opening of their Stoneline Gallery at 132 Wigmore Street. The gallery is set to create a creative hub within the design and art community. Celebrating beautiful objects through collaborations and emerging designers.

title: Miguel Milá: A Life in Design
address: twentytwentyone, 18c River Street, London, EC1R 1XN
verdict: Career retrospective of a mid-century designer. More for design-history fans than teens.
description: Santa & Cole and twentytwentyone present Miguel Milá: A Life in Design, an exhibition celebrating one of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries' most respected designers. Through furniture, lighting, and everyday objects, it explores a lifetime of work defined by ingenuity, craftsmanship, and enduring simplicity.

title: TILE Capsule Collection at Baxter Gallery London
address: Baxter Gallery London, Brompton Road 232-236, Kensington, London, SW3 2BB
verdict: Luxury furniture capsule collection launch. Showroom browsing, low teen pull.
description: Baxter presents TILE, a limited-edition capsule collection designed by the creative duo Draga&Aurel.

title: Delusion: A Cross-Sensory Exhibition
address: Copeland Gallery, Unit 9, Copeland Park, 133 Copeland Rd, London, London, SE15 3SN
verdict: Synaesthesia-inspired show with audio-reactive visuals and optical effects. Sounds genuinely trippy and immersive.
description: Delusions is a cross-sensory exhibition built from synaesthesia and visual snow syndrome. Composited photographs, a live audio-reactive point cloud, layered optical surfaces, stone sheets diffusing sound and scent in place of wall text, and exploration in vermouth extend the work across sight, sound, touch and smell.

title: A living, live-in archive
address: The Atterbury Flat, Atterbury Flat, Chelsea College of Arts, 16 John Islip St, London, SW1P 4JU
verdict: A reimagined flat holding over 100 objects as a live-in archive. Voyeuristic, novel concept, short visit.
description: This September, University of the Arts London presents the Atterbury Flat - a first-of-its-kind living/live-in archive. Housed within a reimagined two-bedroom flat, it brings together over 100 objects and works by UAL students and graduates, creating a home that is both functional and full of character.

title: Strata — 1:4:9 Open Studio
address: Unit 2B, Riverbank Wharf, Riverbank Business Park, London, E3 2TB
verdict: Open studio showing pellet-based 3D printing in action. Seeing the process live is genuinely engaging for tech-curious teens.
description: STRATA is an open studio presentation by 1:4:9 exploring pellet-based 3D printing through a new series of transparent lighting objects, material experiments and works in progress.

title: sensommar
address: Asket Store, 72-74 Brewer Street, London, W1F 9TU
verdict: A scent-led installation, quick and unusual. Good five-minute detour for something different.
description: Asket presents: sensommar, an olfactive installation by DENIM—SYKES. A study in scent, movement and material.

title: ANIMISM OBJECTS -Japan Artisans Design-
address: Pick Store, 64 Charlotte Road, Shoreditch, EC2A 3PE
verdict: Traditional Japanese materials reworked into sound-making objects. Novel and a bit nerdy-cool.
description: Listening to Washi, Aizome, and Yakisugi — New Speakers Shaped by Centuries-Old Craftsmanship. The approach of instilling human and spiritual qualities into objects is deeply rooted in Japanese design thinking. Through ANIMISM, technology, craft, material, and ritual converge in a unified design.

title: Amalgam
address: 14 HANBURY STREET, 14 HANBURY STREET, London, E16QR
verdict: Jewellery and craft made with AI and digital tools. Novel mash-up, good for tech-curious teens.
description: AMALGAM brings together contemporary jewellery, craft and digital practices, exploring how material experimentation, technology and AI are reshaping adornment today. Bringing together international artists and designers, the exhibition moves between physical objects and digital environments.

title: Reviving Craft: Reflection of the Mind
address: Somerset House, Embankment Galleries, South Wing, Strand, London, WC2R 1LA
verdict: Chinese and international craft in a grand courtyard venue. Good quality, calm pace.
description: This Special Project for LDF26 brings together Chinese and international artisans and designers to explore how traditional craftsmanship can be reimagined for contemporary life.

title: (BE)LONGING/S 2.0: Phosphate of Calcium Exhibition
address: hARTslane Gallery, 17 Harts Lane, NEW CROSS GATE, London, SE14 5UP
verdict: Immersive group show on home and displacement in a converted garage. Atmospheric but conceptual.
description: (BE)LONGING/S Project presents an immersive group exhibition exploring notions of  ‘home’, the uncanny, and displacement. Hosted at hARTslane Gallery—a former motorbike garage in New Cross Gate—the show transforms raw industrial architecture into unexpected domestic landscapes.

title: An International Contemporary Art Exhibition: For a Little While
address: Aspara Studio, 200 Battersea Park Rd, London SW11 4ND, London, SW11 4ND
verdict: Standard contemporary art gallery show. Fine if nearby, not worth a special trip.
description: An International Contemporary Art Exhibition Presented by ArtOrb × Apsara Studio Gallery

title: CROSS SECTION - KINGSTON UNIVERSITY
address: Indra Gallery, 20 East Road, London, N1 6AT
verdict: Graduate degree show from Kingston University. Standard student showcase, short two-hour window.
description: CROSS SECTION, by Kingston University's 2026 graduates, brings together emerging designers working across product and furniture design.

title: Resonance Group Exhibition
address: 67 York Street Gallery, 67A York St, London, London, W1H 1QB
verdict: Standard gallery group show. Fine if nearby.
description: Resonance is a group exhibition presented by FAYA Contemporary in collaboration with London Design Festival 2026, taking place at 67 York Street Gallery from 18–21 September 2026.

title: Spotlight: GLAS, PLEXI
address: Siegfried Contemporary, 16 Bassett Road, London, W10 6JJ
verdict: Gallery show of glass and acrylic sculpture. Fine as a passing stop.
description: Andreas Siegfried is debuting a striking new body of work by Paola Petrobelli. Developed in collaboration with CASA YALI, the launch coincides with Petrobelli’s solo show at CASA YALI during Venice Glass Week. Conceived as modular systems, the components of each work can be recombined into many diverse configurations.

title: SCP Clerkenwell Green
address: SCP Clerkenwell Green, 16 Clerkenwell Green, London, EC1R 0QT
verdict: Furniture brand opening a new showroom. Only for furniture enthusiasts.
description:
This September, join SCP to celebrate a new chapter in our history as we relocate from Shoreditch to Clerkenwell Green. 

To mark the special occasion, SCP is hosting an expansive show across the new showroom, courtyard space and event hosting space located in our adjoining office buildings.

title: Past Made Present
address: Ham House and Garden, Ham House and Garden, Ham Street, London, TW10 7RS
verdict: Graduate furniture design shown inside Ham House's 17th-century rooms and garden. Nice combination of history and design, but out west and a short window.
description: Past Made Present spotlights the next generation of practitioners from Kingston University's MA Product & Furniture Design programme. Inspired by Ham House's remarkable seventeenth-century interiors and gardens, it invites audiences to explore how design can reveal new connections between people, place and history.

title: Pentagram x Deus Ex Machina
address: Osh, The Old Sorting House, 46 Essex Road, London, N1 8LN
verdict: A customised 1965 Mini Cooper plus upcycled streetwear. Cars and clothes: strong teen pull.
description: Pentagram x Deus Ex Machina brings together design, craft and making, from an original 1965 Mini Cooper S featuring Matt Willey’s bold livery to a new collection of products and one-off upcycled garments. Created especially for the exhibition, the pieces reflect a shared commitment to originality and thoughtful design.

title: Duel 1509 racquet - the new fast wellness experience
address: Jolene bakery on Redchurch street, 67 Redchurch Street, Shoreditch, London, E2 7DJ
verdict: Hands-on try-out of a new racquet design. Interactive and physical, good for sporty teens.
description: Try the extraordinary Duel 1509 racquet to experience how its mind-bending design unlocks the pleasure of fast movement.

title: Unveiled - Archaeology of a Wall
address: JOY! Factory, Arch 368 Geffrye Street, London, E28HZ
verdict: Immersive installation imagining street art buried under layers of paint. Shoreditch street-art angle is a strong teen hook.
description: What lies beneath a painted wall? Inspired by the hidden history of Shoreditch's street art, JOY! Collective's immersive installation imagines the unseen artworks buried beneath layers of paint. As light shifts, suspended paintings emerge, disappear and overlap, revealing the archaeology of a wall.

title: Line Station Train
address: The Pickle Factory, 5 New Tannery Way, London, SE1 5EB
verdict: TfL-curated show on wayfinding design across the transport network. Good for teens into maps, transit or graphic design.
description: ‘Line Station Train’ is an exhibition curated by TfL Digital in partnership with place branding and wayfinding company DNCO. The exhibition explores how wayfinding design shapes our perception of time and place and helps us navigate complex, always changing urban environments.

title: Better Living By Design Exhibition & Programme
address: The Heals Building, 8 Alfred Mews, Tottenham Court Road, LONDON, W1 7AA
verdict: Cross-sector design showcase in the old Heals building. Pleasant browse, not thrilling.
description: The Lab W1 is London's newest platform for cross-sector collaboration and co-design, and in support of the launch of Soho as LDF's newest Design District, we've bringing "Better Living By Design" our flagship exhibition and cultural programme to the streets of Soho.

title: Mark+Fold Back to School Stationery Pop-up
address: Mark+Fold Soho Pop-up, 33 Great Windmill Street, London, W1D 7LR
verdict: Stationery pop-up with new pencil cases and paper goods. Fun if your teen is into journaling or stationery, otherwise a quick browse.
description: Mark+Fold goes 'back to school' in Soho with first London-made pencil cases and a Japan-Inspired 2027 Collection, in this rare opportunity to shop the British brand's beautifully-crafted paper goods in person during London Design Festival.

title: 10,000 Rivets
address: APOC Store London, Unit 41 Regent Studio, 8 Andrews Road, London, E8 4QN
verdict: Debut furniture and lighting collection at a design store. Nice if into furniture, otherwise skippable.
description: APOC Store presents 10,000 Rivets, the debut collection of furniture, lighting, and objects by Tom Pearson Studio.

title: Enchanted Matter: On Resonant Objects and the Life of Materials
address: Ox Space, 41 Store Street, London, WC1E 7DB
verdict: Conceptual show about materials and attention. More cerebral than fun.
description: Enchanted Matter begins with enchantment as a way of paying attention to the material world. It invites curiosity and wonder, encouraging us to notice how things move, interact and transform in ways that are not always immediately visible.

title: The Circular City Starts With Community
address: Morris+Company, 215-217 Mare Street, London, E8 3QE
verdict: Exhibition on circular-economy city design. Worth it for sustainability-minded teens.
description: Our new exhibition explores how circular economy principles can reshape the way we design, build, make and live in our cities. At its heart is the idea of a Community Circular Economy Hub (CCE): a place where businesses, materials and communities come together to transform waste into useful resources.

title: Mind × Body: Catalyst Phenomenon Archive
address: Space 4, 21–31 Shacklewell Lane, Dalston, London, E8 2DA
verdict: Archive-style show spanning art, design and research on mind and body. Conceptual, niche appeal.
description: The hand does not merely execute thought; it thinks. Work from practitioners across art, design and research assembles a temporary archive of the moment when mind and body catalyse one another, spanning textiles, print, wearable devices, moving image and XR.

title: L.F. Markey presents System T by Emma Cogné
address: L.Markey Store, 50 Dalston Lane, London, E8 3AH
verdict: Small solo art show inside a clothing store. Only if already in Dalston.
description: This September, as part of London Design Festival, L.F. Markey’s Dalston flagship store presents System T, a solo exhibition by French-born, Belgium-based artist Emma Cogné.

title: Mayfair - The Future of Intelligent Cooking: Nothing Burns. Nothing Boils Over
address: Miele Experience Centre Mayfair, 72 Piccadilly Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8HP
verdict: Miele induction hob and cookware demo. Only for teens curious about kitchen tech.
description:
Discover the Future of Intelligent Cooking.

Join us during LDF to experience Miele's new KM 8000 Induction Hob range and M Sense Cookware. With intelligent temperature control, full-surface induction, and innovative sensor technology, enjoy greater flexibility, precision, and confidence in the kitchen.

title: Living with Art: Art, Connection, and Contemporary Luxury Living
address: Regent's View by Berkeley, Regent's View Sales and Marketing Suite, Emma St, Bethnal Green, London, E2 9AP
verdict: Property sales-suite event styled around art and luxury living. Real-estate marketing, not for teens.
description: How art can transform contemporary living into a space for connection, conversation and shared experience?

title: Known Terrain
address: Annex by Koppel Project, 1 Tiverton St, Elephant & Castle, London, SE1 6NT
verdict: Photo and mixed-media group show on how places become familiar. Worth a look if passing through, not a special trip.
description: Known Terrain explores how places, systems and relationships become familiar over time. Rather than a fixed condition, familiarity is understood as something continually shaped through movement, repetition and exchange. Works examine shifting perspectives, everyday encounters and the landscapes around us.

title: Can AI Help Brands Become Immortal?
verdict: A marketing panel on AI and brand legacy, no physical venue listed. Skip unless your teen is into branding or AI strategy.
description: Can a brand outlive the people who shape it without becoming trapped in its past?

title: The Pangolin Shield
address: Strand, Aldwych, London, WC2R 1ES
verdict: Large public sculpture on a closed-off stretch of Strand. Free, striking, no ticket or timing needed.
description: The Pangolin Shield by Studio Saar and Atelier One, supported by Secure, is a Landmark Project on Strand Aldwych. Inspired by the pangolin, the installation explores colonial legacies, power, ecological exploitation, and the movement of people and beings across borders.

title: London is the Gallery
address: Mayfair Design District
verdict: Self-guided trail through Mayfair storefronts turned galleries. Good if your teen likes exploring on foot.
description: London is the Gallery

title: Half the Sky・Women Worth Remembering
verdict: An interactive AI wall of 24 pioneering women you can question in English or Chinese. Fun to try from a phone, but it is an app, not a place to walk to.
description: Talk with the women who shaped history. Half the Sky is a wall of twenty four pioneering women, each carved in plaster and ready to be asked about her work, in English or Chinese. Free, online, and open throughout the Festival.

title: InResponse : Echo. Matter. Sync
address: Thurloe Place, 35 Thurloe Place, London, SW7 2HP
verdict: Small object-design exhibition. Fine as a passing stop, not a destination.
description: At a time when objects are often mass-produced for ever more sophisticated forms of consumption, the works in this exhibition focus on design as an act of responding first.

title: Basic Forms: Reimagining Public Space | In-conversation with Päivi Raivio  and Tim Gill
verdict: Screening and talk on playful public space design. The site lists no fixed time slot, check the Barbican page before travelling.
description: Join artist and designer  Päivi Raivio and author Tim Gill for a screening and conversation on playful urban design
excluded_reason: No fixed time published for 20 Sept — check the venue's own listing before travelling.
